summary: Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Königsberg (~1710–1716) and under Christoph Theodosius Walther. He held posts at Königsberg (~1718–1726) and was later a professor at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (1726).

Specializing in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Leitner studied at King's College London, Freiburg, and Heidelberg. He held posts at King's College, was principal of Oriental College and Government College Lahore, and founded the Oriental Institute, Woking.

Gouriswar Bhattacharya worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Alfred Bloch (~1963–1967) and served as a Lehrbeauftragter at the Free University of Berlin (~1975–1989).

Govind Chandra Pande worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya (~1943–1947). He served as vice-chancellor at Rajasthan (1974–1977), professor at Allahabad (1978–1984), and chairman of the Allahabad Museum and IIAS.

Govind Kumar Meena works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya (2015–2016) and earned his doctorate at Banaras Hindu University (2017–2021). In 2022, he became an assistant professor at Government College University, Lahore.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye was an Indologist and sociologist. He studied at Bahauddin College, Elphinstone College, and Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and Alfred Cort Haddon. He served as head of sociology at the University of Mumbai (1924–1959).

Govind Swamirao Gai worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and linguistics. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India (attested 1958–1967) and the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), later consulting for the American Institute of Indian Studies (attested 1986).

Govind Vinayak Devasthali was an Indologist who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar (attested 1944). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts & RYK Science College (attested 1944) and as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist. He served as a professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1933–1939) and later as director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1953–1957).
Grace Constant Lounsbery was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bryn Mawr College (~1895–1899). She founded Les Amis du Bouddhisme in 1929 and served as its president from 1929 until 1964.

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Morley studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Paris. She directed the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (1934–1958) and the National Museum, New Delhi (1960–1966), and headed the International Council of Museums (1967–1978).

Grace S. Fong is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia (~1978–1984). She served as a professor at Smith College (~1984–1989) and as associate professor and department chair at McGill University (~1989–2020).
Grace Sturtevant Hopkins was a linguist who graduated from Vassar College (~1920–1924). She later earned her Ph.D. at Yale University (~1928–1932), where she studied under Edgar Howard Sturtevant.

Graeme MacQueen was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1972–1979) under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi and held a post as a lecturer at McMaster University (~1977–1989).

Grafton Elliot Smith was an Australian scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Sydney, Sydney Medical School (~1888–1892), and St John's College (~1896–1899), later holding a post at University College London (~1919–1936).
Graham E. Clarke worked in tibetology and other fields. He held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and was a Senior Member at the University of Oxford (attested 1998).
Graham Lock is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and linguistics. He studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Parkes is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who earned his Ph.D. from UC Berkeley (~1974–1978). He held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1979–2008), University College Cork (~2008–2013), and the University of Vienna (2017).

Graham Priest specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge, the London School of Economics under John Lane Bell, and Melbourne, he held appointments at the University of Melbourne, the University of St Andrews, and the Graduate Center, CUNY.

Graham Sandberg was a scholar in tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1866–1870) and Inner Temple (~1870–1874), later serving as a chaplain for the Government of India (1885–1904).
